native_result.query: How were the phases of the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE) characterized in terms of the first principal component in a PCA on the forms of capital analyzed in hundred-year time slices?
native_result.HypoA: During the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE), both phases are primarily associated with negative values on the first principal component (PC1). This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: Both the Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE) were characterized by persistently negative scores along the first principal component (PC1, 31.8% explained variance), reflecting the dominance of traditional Neolithic communal, lithic, and ceramic capital over Bronze Age individual metal prestige capital. The Middle Neolithic exhibited the lowest PC1 scores (mean -1.43, dropping to -1.85 at 3200 BCE) driven by peak stone axe and ceramic diversity, whereas the Younger Neolithic shifted to moderately less negative values (mean -1.18) with notable pulses at 2700 BCE (monument surge) and 2300 BCE (initial daggers and metallurgy).
native_result.WorkflowB: 1. Preprocessed capital.csv with European comma decimals. 2. Performed SVD/PCA on the 12 capital indicators across 100-year slices. 3. Evaluated component loadings and reconstructed time series scores for MN and SG phases.
